summary: Read the retained receipt for the view-lag experiment (CheckRun 24679b2ecdd54556adf91882ce0f8b0c, exit 0): all three runs converged within 0-21ms for every node including the demoted one, and no node's view was still old at a sample where its own LastIndex had reached the configuration entry (stale_max_last_index never above 2 against a configuration index of 3), so the only stale samples were the ones taken before the entry arrived. The six comparisons could not be evaluated because my admission declaration was malformed: the prerequisite was a single per-run baseline event with no role while each demotion_view event carries identity (case, role), which the framework reported as an ambiguous prerequisite association. Submitted a declared successor (previous_id = 244fe01a841341c5a918142383abe8ea-experiment) that changes only the emitted admission shape to one node_baseline event per node and run plus matching prerequisites; construction, timing, sampling and measured fields are unchanged, and the fresh execution is required by that admission change. Native local execution of the fixed harness already emits the per-identity baseline events correctly. The interpretation will follow the receipt.
